analysis.title: UBS Daily Consumer/Lux 26 Oct: Weekly; ABI; Heineken; Brazil Elections; Tesco; Essity; Korea
key_insights: Markets on 26 Oct: Estoxx +35bps, US futures +20-30bps, 10yr back below 5%, Brent down 1.6% toward $114 as Qatari mediators visit Tehran and Trump frames the choice as deal or renewed strikes.

Brazil is the major idiosyncratic risk after Lula's surprise election win (a Brazil ETF listed in Japan fell 16%). Markets will watch fiscal signals: public debt near 90% of GDP and interest costs at 7-8% of GDP (2027 UBSe). Signposts are the finance minister announcement in December, early fiscal signals before Carnival and the March bi-monthly fiscal report.
Moody's kept France at Aa3 and avoided the expected downgrade, giving small relief to French risk.

Week ahead is binary: Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon need to show cloud growth and operating cash flow keep pace with capex after Meta's cash-flow disappointment. FOMC is Wednesday, ECB Thursday, BoJ Friday. 46% of SPY and 38% of QQQ market cap reports.

AI/compute: Musk warned of 'stranded compute' in partially complete data centers, while AWS says large blocks of capacity are committed through 2027 and into 2028. The desk's view is that operational compute stays scarce while poorly executed or financed capacity gets stranded.

EU trading desk (George Redman) is constructive that the AI financing premium can fade if hyperscaler results deliver, after substantial de-grossing and systematic selling. Bull case is hyperscaler cash flow plus stable oil, risk is stranded capital meeting renewed geopolitical escalation. Tactical opportunity may sit lower in the capacity chain, in less crowded European industrials and infrastructure.

Oil is the macro constraint. A credible Iran deal would be the cleanest catalyst for lower inflation expectations, calmer rates and broader equity participation, and renewed hostilities would likely reverse all three. US midterms are just over a week away.

Friday flow was balanced (51/49) with turnover near 2x the YTD average. Industrials were the busiest sector (20% of turnover, better for sale in A&D), Financials saw strong demand (exchanges), Consumer Discretionary was better bid (personal care, eyewear).
Weekly: Food/Bevs YTD +13.5% outperformed the SXXP by 310bps on the week. HPC/Tob/Lux YTD -6.4% outperformed by 70bps. Staples outperformed in a defensive rotation (SX3P +2.1%, SXQP +0.9%).

Luxury Q3 shows polarisation. Hermès (Sell) missed at group level at 4% and UBS cut PT 2% to €1,150, with consensus +7% cFX growth in 2027 seen as high. Kering (N) Gucci retail missed at -9% vs -6% consensus, and UBS cut FY26/27/28 EPS 7%/2%/3%. Kering was the worst luxury performer at -16.57%.
Zegna (Buy) beat with +8% OSG vs +7% consensus and DTC +16%, supporting up to 2% EPS upgrades. EssilorLuxottica (Buy) beat with >6% cFX core growth, DTC +10.6% and APAC +15.7%.

Frasers Group crossed 50.08% of Hugo Boss (34.5m shares) and will consolidate it. The move does not trigger a new mandatory offer since the German 30% threshold was already crossed. Frasers also holds sold puts on up to 15.1m shares (21.87%).
Sportswear: Deckers (Buy) fell 7% after hours on softer HOKA/UGG trends and an FY27 sales guide-down. Puma appointed ANTA M&A head Dennis Tao as Supervisory Board Chair.

Retail: Sainsbury 1H EBIT +3.6% to £525m, in line, and raised the lower end of EBIT guidance to £1,025m. Carrefour (Neutral) cut FY26 EBIT 5% on weak September France trends and was downgraded to Neutral. Tesco equal pay case goes back to the Tribunal after the Supreme Court rejected a procedural appeal, which does not determine liability.

Beverages: Crown Q3 volumes +6% (Brazil +4%, SE Asia +mid-teens, Mexico -1%) are a positive read-across to ABI and Heineken. Germany's proposed sugar tax is a potential headwind for CCEP, needing c22% pricing for full pass-through.

Food & HPC: L'Oréal Q3 LFL +7.7% vs 5.4% consensus (PT +6% to €465). Galderma beat Q3 sales by 5% and raised FY26 growth guidance to 22.5-23.5% from 19-21%. Essity (Sell) Q3 OSG -0.3% vs +1.2% consensus, EBITA margin -150bps to 13.1%.

Tobacco: PMI Q3 beat on combustibles, FY26 organic sales growth lifted to +6.3%, PT +4% to $201. UK combustibles volumes -11.2% in September, US cigarette imports +40% on a 6mma basis (a potential drawback read-across for Altria/BAT), nicotine pouch imports -62% y/y.

XLP outperformed the S&P by about 265bps WTD, a third straight week of outperformance and more than 11% cumulative, the 3rd-best three-week stretch in 10 years. UBS says much of it is rotation, not fundamentals.

Ross Stores upgraded to Buy from Neutral, PT raised 32% to $315 (37% upside), FY28 EPS 9% above consensus, 15% EPS CAGR. Wolverine (WWW) Q3 preview: UBS expects a 2c beat, options imply +/-9.5% vs 8.6% historical average.
Korea cosmetics: UBS constructive on both brands and ODMs, prefers Cosmecca and Cosmax. APR/d'Alba brands show 36-40% 2026-28E OP CAGR vs 13-19% for ODMs.
Pop Mart Q3 preview: UBS expects revenue -45% YoY, a well-anticipated weak quarter. Xtep Q3 core-brand sales fell mid-single digits, guidance maintained, Buy with HK$5.10 PT.

market_movers.rationale: Upgraded from Neutral, PT raised 32%. Expects store productivity gap with TJX to narrow, about 8.5% annual revenue growth over FY27-FY28, FY28 EPS 9% above consensus.
Hermès Q3 group growth of 4% missed, PT cut 2% on broadening signs of cyclicality, with consensus 2027 growth of +7% cFX seen as leaving little room for error.
Colgate expected to report in line, lower end of +MSD EPS growth more likely given cost pressure.
Trades at about 13x NTM EPS. UBS expects net sales of $26.4B vs $26.3B consensus and EPS of $2.30 in line.
UBS expects 1Q EPS of $1.06 vs $1.10 consensus on commodity and transport cost pressure.
PT lowered from $86. Macro pressure and affordability concerns weigh on same-store sales, plus a leadership transition in January.
Gross margin missed on transportation pressure, but 2027 looks like an earnings recovery year driven by company levers.
Sentiment positive and shares +16% QTD vs XLP +11.6%. Much near-term upside already reflected in valuation.
UBS forecasts a 2c Q3 EPS beat on Saucony and Merrell strength, with potential for an above-average earnings move.
PT raised 4% after a Q3 beat driven by combustibles.
Strong 1Q beat on organic sales and margin, with organic sales likely toward the higher end of the guided range.
Reports 3Q on 10/27. Investors are asking about risk/reward given YTD outperformance, but UBS sees the fundamental gap widening.
Q3 LFL +7.7% vs 5.4% consensus, PT raised 6%.
Q3 EPS beat on margin, but shipments now at the lower end of the range and gross margins near peak.
No major surprises expected, meeting expectations could be enough.
Favored name, focus is on 2027 earnings trajectory.
Modest upside to Street on organic sales and gross margin, debate shifts to 2027 as hedges roll off.
Stronger organic sales growth but category growth remains pressured and input costs weigh on the outlook.
Step-up in pricing could see Altria raise the lower end of the FY26 guide.
Japan Tobacco: 3Q26E EPS +2.6% ahead of consensus, could raise FY26 guidance. PT raised 4.5% from ¥7,800.
Xtep Q3 core-brand sales fell mid-single digits in line, guidance maintained.

sector_views.rationale: Defensive rotation drove staples demand, though hedge fund feedback suggests the tobacco sector could lag as wider staples attract interest.
Q3 shows polarisation: Zegna and EssilorLuxottica beat while Hermès and Kering disappointed. Weak China demand and Christmas trading are the next proof points.
XLP outperformance is driven by rotation, not fundamentals. UBS expects top and bottom line visibility to drive outperformance once volatility fades.
Desk sees tactical opportunity further down the AI capacity chain in less crowded European industrials and infrastructure.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Back below 5%, easing pressure on equities.
Pulled back on Qatari mediation, but remains the macro constraint.
Interest costs of 7-8% of GDP (2027 UBSe) raise the bar for fiscal credibility under Lula.
Weighs on affordability-sensitive retailers such as Sprouts.
Removes an immediate European tail risk.

trade_ideas.rationale: Litigation overhang seen as largely de-risked and core business attractive, UBSe Q3 LFL +4.2% vs consensus +4.1%.

trade_ideas.description: Long Heineken into results, sell into any strength on the day
trade_ideas.rationale: Positioning is light and there is upside risk to volumes across all regions.

trade_ideas.description: Long MICC (Magnum Ice Cream Company) into results
trade_ideas.rationale: Expecting a beat driven by the weather.
UBSe Q3 organic volume/revenue slightly below consensus, no upside in Western Europe, and the company has disappointed against expectations for too long.
Long-side positioning feels heavy so it could become a 'travel and arrive' situation, with Aperitifs more Q2/Q3 weighted so performance could fade in Q4.
trade_ideas.risk: Clean execution on strategy and RTD roll-out could keep investors supportive.

tension_points.bull_case: Desk is constructive that the AI financing premium fades if Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon deliver cash flow, helped by lower oil, sub-5% 10yr yields and prior de-grossing.
tension_points.bear_case: Stranded compute risk and renewed geopolitical escalation could leave leveraged capacity builders unable to prove the economics, after Meta's cash-flow disappointment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler results this week failing to show cloud growth, backlog conversion and operating cash flow keeping pace with capex, or renewed hostilities.

tension_points.bull_case: A credible deal would lower inflation expectations, calm rates and broaden equity participation.
tension_points.bear_case: US military preparations, Trump's comments and Houthi attacks keep renewed strikes in the distribution.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed strikes would reverse lower inflation expectations, calmer rates and broader equity participation.

tension_points.bull_case: XLP has outperformed the S&P by more than 11% over three weeks and top-line visibility should drive outperformance.
tension_points.bear_case: Strength is driven by rotation rather than fundamentals, and input cost inflation puts 2027 EPS at risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rotation reversing or cost inflation hitting guidance in the earnings season.
